description: [Leakage-Safe Walk-Forward Machine-Learning Factor] Produces a LightGBM regression score for each instrument after completed session t, targeting the cross-sectional percentile rank of the adjusted-close return C[t+5]/C[t]-1. Training observations are pooled instrument-days and receive equal weight. At each refit session r, the candidate training feature-date window contains at most 504 global market sessions ending at r-5, so every included five-session forward label is observable by the close of r. description: [Leakage-Safe Residual Liquidity-Pressure Machine-Learning Factor] Produces one raw LightGBM prediction for each instrument after completed session t using exactly four same-date cross-sectional percentile-ranked liquidity-pressure inputs derived from daily_pv.h5: a 5-session mean and a 20-session mean of the sign of the close log return multiplied by clipped log-volume surprise, a 20-session Amihud-style mean absolute close log return divided by close times volume, and the negative one-session close log return multiplied by the positive part of clipped log-volume surprise. A model requires at least 252 distinct eligible feature sessions and is refitted every 20 global market sessions. description: [Leakage-Safe One-Day Price-Structure Machine-Learning Factor] Produces one raw LightGBM prediction for each instrument after completed global market session t. The model uses exactly three predictors: same-date cross-sectional percentile ranks of Overnight_Gap_1D, Close_Location_Value_1D, and Close_Momentum_20D. Its target is the same-date cross-sectional percentile rank of the adjusted close return from feature session s to the exact next global market session, not the next instrument-specific observation. An instrument-day label is included only when the instrument has finite, strictly positive adjusted closes on both s and that exact next global session; a close observed only on a later session cannot substitute for the required endpoint. At refit session r, training uses the most recent at most 504 global feature sessions preceding r whose next-global-session endpoints are observable by the close of r. At least 252 distinct training feature sessions containing a finite label are required. The model is refitted every 5 global sessions, anchored at the first session satisfying that minimum, and remains fixed between refits. Training observations are pooled instrument-days with equal weights. Missing ranked predictors are passed to LightGBM without imputation, while rows with missing labels are excluded. Fixed parameters are objective=regression_l2, learning_rate=0.03, n_estimators=100, num_leaves=4, max_depth=2, min_child_samples=500, subsample=1.0, colsample_bytree=1.0, reg_alpha=0.2, reg_lambda=2.0, random_state=42, and n_jobs=-1, with no early stopping. The saved factor is the untransformed continuous prediction on completed session t, with zero physical row shift. The three retained SOTA factors remain separate and are not re-emitted or replaced by this incremental factor.

description: [Conditioned Overnight Gap-Reversal Factor] Measures the negative of the current overnight gap only when the completed regular session moves in the opposite direction, indicating that the overnight price change was rejected intraday. The overnight gap is clipped to the fixed interval [-0.10, 0.10], and its magnitude is multiplied by a recovery ratio capped at 1, defined as the absolute intraday return divided by the absolute raw overnight gap plus 10^-12. The factor is exactly zero when the overnight gap and intraday return have the same sign, when either return is zero, or when their product is zero. It requires the current adjusted open and close and exactly one immediately preceding instrument-specific adjusted close to be finite and strictly positive. description: [Orthogonalized Price-Structure Dynamics Machine-Learning Factor] Produces a leakage-safe walk-forward LightGBM prediction from exactly 15 predictors constructed from the three retained price-structure signals: Overnight_Gap_1D, Close_Location_Value_1D, and Close_Momentum_20D. Each raw signal is first transformed into an ascending, average-tie, same-date cross-sectional percentile rank over finite observations. For each instrument and prediction session t, the model receives each ranked signal at fixed instrument-specific observation lags 0, 1, 2, 5, and 10; a lagged value retains the percentile rank calculated on its original historical date. The target is the same-feature-date percentile rank of the adjusted-close return from a historical feature session to its exact next global market session. Labels are missing when the instrument lacks finite, strictly positive adjusted closes at either endpoint; a later instrument observation cannot replace a missing exact-next-global-session close. At each refit, the model pools equal-weight instrument-days from at most 504 global feature sessions preceding the refit, including only labels whose exact next-global-session endpoint is observable by that refit. At least 252 distinct eligible feature sessions are required. Refitting occurs every 5 global sessions, anchored at the first eligible refit session, and the fitted model remains fixed between refits. Missing predictors are passed directly to LightGBM without imputation. Fixed parameters are objective=regression_l2, learning_rate=0.02, n_estimators=200, num_leaves=7, max_depth=3, min_child_samples=500, subsample=1.0, colsample_bytree=1.0, reg_alpha=0.2, reg_lambda=2.0, random_state=42, and n_jobs=-1, with no early stopping. On every prediction date, the raw model predictions are regressed cross-sectionally on an intercept and the three current, lag-zero retained-SOTA ranks. The saved output is the resulting residual divided by its same-date population standard deviation. At least 30 rows with a finite prediction and all three finite current SOTA ranks are required; otherwise the entire date is NaN. Rows outside the complete-case residualization universe are NaN, and the entire date is also NaN when the residual population standard deviation is zero or non-finite. description: [Directional Persistence Factor] Measures the balance between positive and negative adjusted-close log returns over exactly 10 consecutive instrument-specific return intervals ending on completed session t. Each positive return contributes 1, each negative return contributes -1, and each exactly zero return contributes 0. The factor is the arithmetic mean of these 10 signs, so valid outputs are bounded to [-1,1] in increments of 0.1. A value near 1 indicates consistently rising closes, a value near -1 indicates consistently falling closes, and a value near 0 indicates balanced, flat, or directionally inconsistent movement. The calculation requires exactly 11 consecutive instrument-specific adjusted closes from positions t-10 through t to be finite and strictly positive. Any invalid close makes the entire output NaN; no partial window, missing-value skipping, filling, clipping, ranking, winsorization, or normalization is allowed. The factor uses only the $close column of daily_pv.h5. It has zero physical row shift, remains indexed on completed session t, and may be used only for prediction targets or holding periods beginning after t. The three retained Trial 2 SOTA factors remain separate and are not re-implemented or re-emitted.

description: [Multi-Horizon Walk-Forward Ridge Replacement Factor] Compresses the three validated Trial 2 price-structure signals into one leakage-safe standalone replacement score. The predictors are ascending, average-tie, same-date cross-sectional percentile ranks of Overnight_Gap_1D, Close_Location_Value_1D, and Close_Momentum_20D at fixed instrument-specific observation lags 0, 1, 2, 5, and 10, producing exactly 15 predictors. A lagged predictor retains the percentile rank calculated on its original historical date. The training target is the equal-weight arithmetic mean of three cross-sectional forward-return percentile ranks measured at exact global-session horizons 1, 3, and 5. Each horizon requires a finite, strictly positive adjusted close on both the feature date and its exact global-session endpoint; a later instrument observation cannot replace a missing endpoint. At each refit, training candidates come from at most 504 global feature sessions strictly preceding the refit date. A row is retained only when all 15 predictors and all three horizon labels are finite and every label endpoint is observable by the refit date. At least 252 distinct feature sessions containing one or more retained rows are required. The model is refitted every 5 global sessions, anchored at the first eligible refit date, and remains fixed between refits. Ridge parameters are fixed at alpha=100, fit_intercept=true, solver=lsqr, tol=1e-6, and max_iter=1000. All retained instrument-day rows have equal weight. On each prediction date, raw predictions are generated only for rows with all 15 finite predictors and are converted into ascending, average-tie, same-date cross-sectional percentile ranks. The ranked prediction is saved with zero physical row shift and no clipping, winsorization, residualization, calibration, or additional normalization. This factor is intended to replace, rather than augment, the three retained factors in the standalone evaluation; Overnight_Gap_1D, Close_Location_Value_1D, and Close_Momentum_20D are not separately re-emitted by this output.

description: [Twenty-Session Price-Range Position Factor] Measures the position of the current adjusted close within the full adjusted high-low envelope observed over exactly 20 consecutive completed instrument-specific sessions ending on session t. The lower boundary is the minimum adjusted low and the upper boundary is the maximum adjusted high across positions t-19 through t. Values near 1 indicate that the current close is near the persistent 20-session high, while values near 0 indicate that it is near the persistent 20-session low. The factor requires all 20 adjusted highs and all 20 adjusted lows, together with the current adjusted close, to be finite and strictly positive. The resulting 20-session range must also be finite and strictly positive. Exactly 20 consecutive instrument-specific observations are required; no partial window, missing-value skipping, filling, interpolation, ranking, clipping, winsorization, normalization, or additional transformation is allowed. Under internally consistent OHLC data, valid values lie in [0,1], but the output is not clipped if source-data inconsistencies place it outside this interval. The factor uses only the $high, $low, and $close columns of daily_pv.h5. description: [Walk-Forward Cross-Sectional LambdaRank Replacement Factor] Produces a leakage-safe LightGBM LambdaRank score using only the three validated Trial 2 price-structure signals: Overnight_Gap_1D, Close_Location_Value_1D, and Close_Momentum_20D. Each source signal is independently converted into an ascending, average-tie, same-date cross-sectional percentile rank over its finite observations, yielding exactly three predictors with no historical predictor lags. The training label is an ordinal value in {0,1,2,3,4} representing the cross-sectional quintile of the adjusted-close return from a historical feature session to its exact next global market session. Label quintiles are calculated independently by feature date using ascending average-tie return ranks; larger next-session returns receive larger labels. A label is missing unless the instrument has finite, strictly positive adjusted closes on both the feature date and the exact next global session. A later instrument observation cannot replace a missing exact endpoint. At each refit, candidate feature dates are the most recent at most 504 global sessions strictly preceding the refit date. A training row requires a finite ordinal label and all three finite ranked predictors, and its label endpoint must be no later than the refit date. Retained rows are ordered by feature date and supplied to LambdaRank as date-level query groups, so ranking loss is optimized only within each historical cross section. At least 252 distinct feature sessions contributing one or more retained rows are required. The first model is fitted on the first eligible global session, and subsequent refits occur every 5 global sessions from that anchor; the fitted model remains unchanged between refits. Fixed LightGBM parameters are objective=lambdarank, label_gain=[0,1,2,3,4], learning_rate=0.03, n_estimators=100, num_leaves=7, max_depth=3, min_child_samples=200, subsample=1.0, colsample_bytree=1.0, reg_alpha=0.2, reg_lambda=2.0, random_state=42, and n_jobs=-1, with no early stopping. On each prediction date, raw predictions are generated only for instruments with all three finite predictors and are converted into ascending, average-tie, same-date percentile ranks. The ranked prediction is saved on completed session t with zero physical row shift. No clipping, winsorization, residualization, calibration, sign reversal, or further normalization is applied. This score is intended for standalone replacement screening rather than incremental addition; the three retained Trial 2 factors remain unchanged and are not separately emitted.

description: [Volatility-Scaled Overnight Price Discovery Factor] Measures the current overnight simple return relative to the instrument's realized high-low range volatility over exactly 20 prior completed instrument-specific sessions. The numerator is the adjusted open on session t divided by the adjusted close at the immediately preceding instrument-specific observation minus one. The denominator is the square root of the mean squared logarithmic high-low range over positions t-20 through t-1, excluding all current-session high, low, and close information. The standardized gap is clipped to the fixed interval [-3,3] to limit the influence of adjustment artifacts and extreme opening moves. A valid value requires the current open, previous close, and all 20 prior highs and lows to be finite and strictly positive, every prior high to be strictly greater than its corresponding low, and the resulting volatility denominator to be finite and strictly positive. Exactly 20 prior instrument-specific sessions are required; no partial window, missing-value skipping, filling, interpolation, ranking, winsorization, annualization, or additional normalization is allowed. The factor uses only the $open, $close, $high, and $low columns of daily_pv.h5, has zero physical row shift, and remains indexed on completed session t. It is intended as a controlled one-for-one replacement for Overnight_Gap_1D while Close_Location_Value_1D and Close_Momentum_20D remain unchanged; it must not be appended as a fourth feature in the replacement test.

description: [Walk-Forward Participation-Regime Machine-Learning Factor] Produces a leakage-safe LightGBM score from exactly five same-date cross-sectional percentile-ranked inputs derived from adjusted close and volume data: Lagged_VolumeChange_Return_Correlation_20D reconstructed solely as a model input, lagged log-volume surprise measured at t-1 against the 20 observations from t-21 through t-2, the current close log return, 20-session realized close volatility ending at t, and 20-session mean Amihud-style illiquidity ending at t. Each raw input is independently transformed into an ascending, average-tie percentile rank within its exact feature date. The target is the ascending same-feature-date percentile rank of the adjusted-close return from feature session G_k to the exact next global session G_{k+1}; a later instrument observation cannot replace a missing exact endpoint. At each refit, training uses at most the 504 most recent global feature sessions strictly preceding the refit date, retains only complete rows whose exact label endpoint is observable by the refit, and requires at least 252 distinct eligible feature sessions. The first model is fitted on the first eligible global session, subsequent scheduled refits occur every 5 global sessions from that anchor, and the fitted model remains fixed between refits. Fixed LightGBM parameters are objective=regression_l2, learning_rate=0.02, n_estimators=150, num_leaves=7, max_depth=3, min_child_samples=500, subsample=1.0, colsample_bytree=1.0, reg_alpha=0.2, reg_lambda=2.0, random_state=42, and n_jobs=-1, with no early stopping. Raw predictions are generated only for instruments having all five finite current predictors and are converted into ascending, average-tie, same-date percentile ranks. This ranked prediction is the single output, indexed on completed session t with zero physical shift. No clipping, winsorization, residualization, sign reversal, calibration, or additional normalization is applied. The factor must be evaluated standalone before any possible incremental test. Overnight_Gap_1D, Close_Location_Value_1D, and Close_Momentum_20D remain retained unchanged and are not re-emitted; Lagged_VolumeChange_Return_Correlation_20D remains excluded as a standalone library factor and is reconstructed only as an internal predictor.

description: [Five-Session Smoothed Lagged Price-Participation Correlation Factor] Computes five consecutive 20-pair Pearson correlations between one-interval-lagged log-volume changes and subsequent adjusted-close log returns, then combines them using the fixed weights 0.40, 0.25, 0.15, 0.12, and 0.08 for correlation endpoints t through t-4, respectively. For a correlation ending at session s, each pair indexed by d uses ln(V[d-1]/V[d-2]) and ln(C[d]/C[d-1]) for exactly 20 endpoints d=s-19 through s. All means, variances, standard deviations, and covariances use population moments with divisor 20 and ddof=0. A valid output requires all five component correlations to be valid and therefore requires exactly 26 consecutive instrument-specific adjusted closes and volumes from t-25 through t to be finite and strictly positive. Each component additionally requires finite, strictly positive population standard deviations for both of its 20-observation series and a finite resulting correlation. If any source value or component correlation is invalid, the smoothed output is NaN. No partial smoothing, weight renormalization, missing-value filling, interpolation, clipping, winsorization, ranking, residualization, or additional normalization is applied. The factor uses only the $close and $volume columns of daily_pv.h5, has zero physical output shift, remains indexed on completed session t, and may be aligned only with prediction targets or holding periods beginning after t. Overnight_Gap_1D, Close_Location_Value_1D, and Close_Momentum_20D remain retained unchanged and are not re-implemented or re-emitted. This factor must be tested standalone first; an incremental test with the unchanged SOTA factors is permitted only if standalone IC remains strictly above 0.019438 and after-cost return, turnover, and maximum drawdown improve materially under identical controls.

description: [Liquidity-Stress Acceleration Factor] Measures the logarithmic change in Amihud-style liquidity stress between the most recent five completed instrument-specific sessions and the immediately preceding 20 completed sessions. Session-level stress is the absolute adjusted-close log return divided by adjusted close times trading volume. The recent mean uses exactly the five endpoints t-4 through t, while the preceding mean uses exactly the 20 endpoints t-24 through t-5; the windows are disjoint. A valid output requires exactly 26 consecutive instrument-specific observations from t-25 through t, with every adjusted close and volume finite and strictly positive. Both fixed-window stress means and their ratio must be finite and strictly positive. If any source value, intermediate stress value, mean, ratio, or final logarithm is invalid, the output is NaN. No partial windows, missing-value skipping, filling, interpolation, denominator stabilizer, clipping, winsorization, ranking, residualization, or additional normalization is applied. The factor uses only the $close and $volume columns of daily_pv.h5, has zero physical row shift, remains indexed on completed session t, and may be aligned only with prediction targets or holding periods beginning after t. Overnight_Gap_1D, Close_Location_Value_1D, and Close_Momentum_20D remain retained unchanged and are not re-implemented or re-emitted. This factor must first be evaluated standalone, including IC, ICIR, temporal stability, coverage, turnover, gross and after-cost return, transaction-cost sensitivity, quantile behavior, and maximum drawdown. An incremental test with the retained SOTA factors is permitted only if the standalone predictive and portfolio diagnostics are favorable.

description: [Exponentially Weighted Lagged Price-Participation Correlation Factor] Measures the weighted Pearson correlation over exactly 20 pairs between the prior-session log-volume change and the immediately subsequent adjusted-close log return. Pair lag i=0 is the newest pair, using ln(V[t-1]/V[t-2]) with ln(C[t]/C[t-1]); pair lag i=19 is the oldest pair. Fixed normalized weights are proportional to 2^(-i/10), giving a half-life of exactly 10 instrument-specific sessions and greater influence to recent observations. Weighted means, variances, standard deviations, and covariance all use the same normalized weights. A valid output requires exactly 22 consecutive instrument-specific observations from t-21 through t, with every adjusted close and volume finite and strictly positive. Both weighted population standard deviations and their product must be finite and strictly positive, and the resulting correlation must be finite. Any invalid source value, incomplete window, non-finite intermediate value, or zero standard deviation produces NaN. No partial windows, missing-value skipping, filling, interpolation, denominator stabilizer, clipping, winsorization, ranking, residualization, or normalization beyond that intrinsic to the weighted Pearson correlation is applied. Only the $close and $volume columns of daily_pv.h5 are used. The output has zero physical row shift, remains indexed on completed session t, and may be aligned only with targets or holding periods beginning after t. Overnight_Gap_1D, Close_Location_Value_1D, and Close_Momentum_20D remain retained unchanged and are not re-implemented or re-emitted.
